newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ABARE sees chance of 4th Australian rate cut.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ABARE sees chance of 4th Australian rate cut.

text.p: The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Tuesday that Australian banks' prime lending rate might fall further, in part because the Reserve Bank might ease monetary policy again.

The central bank's cut in overnight cash rates to 6.0 percent last week had left Australian banks' real prime lending rates (nominal rates less inflation) at about seven percent, which was high compared with other countries.

"Given the outlook for continued low inflation and increased competition in the banking sector, there are prospects for further reductions in Australia's prime lending rates," the bureau said in its quarterly Australian Commodities publication.
However, its commodities forecasts assumed stable prime rates, the bureau said.
The bank has now cut interest rates on three consecutive occasions, beginning in July when it dropped its cash rate target to 7.0 percent from 7.5 percent.
The bureau assumed that the Australian dollar would average US$0.7800 in 1996/97, compared with US$0.7600 in 1995/96.
Around the midsession on Tuesday, the Australian dollar was trading at US$0.7925.
The currency would average 57.9 points on the Reserve Bank's trade weighted index this fiscal year, up from 54.8 previously.
The bureau forecast 3.3 percent year-average GDP growth for 1996/97, compared with the Treasury's August budget forecast of 3.5 percent and the 1995/96 outcome of 4.3 percent.
"In the short term, growth in private consumption expenditure is assumed to strengthen gradually in response to lower domestic interest rates," it said.
Export performance would also remain strong but relatively weak public sector spending would hold down the growth rate.

It also forecast slightly higher inflation for 1996/97 -- a 2.1 percent rise in the average consumer price index from the previous year, compared with the budget forecast of 2.0 percent and the 1995/96 result of 4.2 percent.
